text: A deploy script in Foundry is itself a Solidity contract — reviewable, testable, versioned — instead of a sequence of cast send commands nobody can reproduce exactly.
Running the script with no flags simulates it — no transaction sent, catching a broken constructor argument before it costs real gas. Adding broadcast and rpc-url actually sends it.
A raw private-key flag puts a plaintext key into shell history. Foundry's recommended alternative is a keystore account — encrypted on disk, prompting for a password only at broadcast time.
rpc_endpoints turns a long URL into a short alias. One real gotcha: chain only sets block.chainid inside the simulation — rpc-url is what actually controls the destination network.
The script simulates, broadcasts, and can even verify in the same command. Lesson 14 goes deep on that verification step — what it actually publishes, and why.
